trustlines.pageSubtitle: Learn how trustlines work on the Stellar network
trustlines.whatAreContent: Trustlines are explicit opt-in mechanisms on the Stellar network. They allow an account to hold and receive specific tokens issued by other accounts. Without a trustline, an account cannot receive any non-native asset.
trustlines.whyExistContent: Trustlines exist as a security feature. They prevent spam tokens from being sent to your account without your consent. This is fundamentally different from networks like Ethereum where any token can be sent to any address. On Stellar, you must explicitly trust an asset before receiving it.
trustlines.howToActivateContent: To activate a trustline, you need to submit a Change Trust operation to the Stellar network. This requires signing a transaction with your account's secret key.
trustlines.whichToTrustContent: Only trust tokens from verified issuers. Check the issuer's stellar.toml file and verify the domain. Well-known issuers include Circle (USDC, EURC) and the SDF. On testnet, the issuer for test USDC/EURC is the SDF's standard test issuer.
trustlines.practicalExampleContent: To receive USDC on testnet: 1) Fund your account with Friendbot (10,000 XLM), 2) Add a trustline for USDC using the test issuer above, 3) Request USDC from this faucet. Your account will then show both XLM and USDC balances.
trustlines.summaryWhatBrief: Trustlines let your Stellar account hold non-native tokens like USDC and EURC. Without one, you can't receive these assets.
trustlines.summaryWhy: Why do I need one for USDC/EURC?
trustlines.summaryWhyBrief: Stellar requires explicit opt-in before receiving tokens. This protects you from unwanted spam tokens. Add a trustline to start receiving stablecoins.
